contentBlocks.body: Partial, Required, and Readonly are not magic: they are mapped types, written with the [K in keyof T] syntax that loops over the keys of T. You can write your own to derive form state, error maps, or feature flags from a single source type, so adding a field in one place updates all of them.

Modifiers can be added or removed: ? makes a key optional, -? removes optionality (that is how Required works), readonly and -readonly do the same for readonly. You can also rename keys with as and template literal types, for example { [K in keyof T as `set${Capitalize<string & K>}`]: (value: T[K]) => void } builds setter names.

When you build a mapped-type object at runtime with a loop, TypeScript cannot follow the loop, so you usually start from {} as Flags<T> and assign key by key. Keep that cast local to one small helper.

knowledgeItems.prompt: What does { [K in keyof T]?: T[K] } produce?

payload.explanation: It maps each key K of T to the same value type T[K], adding the ? modifier. That is exactly how Partial is defined.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Which modifier inside a mapped type removes optionality, as Required<T> does?

payload.explanation: Required<T> is { [K in keyof T]-?: T[K] }. The minus removes the modifier.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Compare a form's original and edited values: return a Flags<T> map of which keys changed and a Partial<T> patch with only the changed values.
